_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 2 Computing unit lecture film, Lesson 6 Bee-Bot Journeys. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON[lecture] in order: the floor robot and its buttons; CLEAR then GO (with the deepened part on why you clear first folded in); one press one square; a destination with a wall in the way; predicting before GO; robots at work. THE GRID IS DRAWN BY THE FILM, because the lesson keeps Robo's grid inside a closure - but every direction, turn and angle comes from ART.robo (DIRS, TURN_L, TURN_R, ANGLE) and every route is one of the lesson's own levels: Journey 1 (F F F to the shop), Journey 2 (F F R F F to the house), Journey 4 (F L F R F F R F round the wall to school) and Program 1 of the predictor (F F L F from column 1 row 1 facing down).
title: Bee-Bot Journeys
subtitle: Grade 2 Computing
objectives: Know how to enter directional instructions in to a physical computing device to enable it to reach a specific destination.

beats.say: A floor robot drives on a grid of squares on the floor.
Press its buttons, press GO, and off it goes to the shop.
This is a floor robot. It drives on a grid of squares.
On its back are buttons: forward, backwards, turn left, turn right.
The shop is three squares ahead, so press forward three times.
Every press is remembered, in order. That list is the program.
Press GO, and it runs them all, one square at a time.
The robot keeps every press you make until you clear it.
Press CLEAR first. That wipes the old program away.
Forget CLEAR, and your new presses join on to the old ones.

at.join: join on to the old ones

beats.say: The robot sets off doing both, and stops in the wrong place.
It is not confused. So clear it, enter the presses, then GO.
Each press of the forward button moves the robot one square.
Each turn spins it a quarter turn. It does not move at all.
Count the squares. The house is two up, then two to the right.
Forward, forward, turn right, forward, forward: five presses.
Press GO, and the robot drives all the way to the house.
Every journey has a destination: the shop, home, school.
This time a wall is in the way. You cannot drive through it.

at.wall: a wall is in the way

beats.say: Turn before you reach it, and go round it to the school.
Forward, turn left, forward. Turn right, forward, forward.
Turn right, then forward, and the robot is at school.
Before you press GO, follow the program in your head.
Move your finger one square for every forward press.
This robot faces down. Forward, forward: two squares down.
Turn left. It faces right now, but it has not moved.
One more forward, and your finger is on the shop.
Now press GO, and the robot stops on the shop too.
Big robots follow the same kind of program as yours.
A warehouse robot drives to shelf fourteen, then stops.
A hospital robot turns left at the right ward door.
A robot vacuum turns when it bumps. A delivery robot finds house numbers.
The buttons on its back make up the program.
CLEAR first, then all the presses, then GO.
One press is one square. A turn only spins.
Predict where it will stop, then press GO and see.
